decisions.reason: As a renamed and modularized version of the already well-liked BASIC 518 with its own dedicated page, it looks like an extension of a proven line rather than a weak experiment.
The dedicated page and strong fit with the firm's mobile waste-processing portfolio mean the option still has meaningful upside and too little negative evidence after only one year to justify exit.
Website presence is limited, but it builds on existing mobile grinder capabilities and in this machinery business one year is usually too early to conclude that market potential is not there.

Although only briefly mentioned so far, a stationary electric fine shredder fits the firm's push toward tougher and more resource-saving processing solutions, so management would likely keep the option open.

This green-waste variant appears more niche and has weak public market evidence, but it likely shares platforms and know-how with other grinders, making it relatively inexpensive to keep on offer while demand becomes clearer.
A dedicated page and close adjacency to the firm's established stationary shredding and recycling systems suggest enough strategic coherence and option value to continue rather than withdraw quickly.
